entries.title: Uranium Finance is drained of $50 million in hack
entries.body: A bug in Uranium Finance, a <button class="define-target" id="defi">DeFi</button> exchange based on Binance Smart Chain, allowed an attacker to drain the <button class="define-target" id="liquidity-pool">liquidity pools</button> for multiple token pairs. Uranium had just commissioned an <button class="define-target" id="audit">audit</button> which uncovered the bug, but the attack occured two hours before the patch went live. An apparent member of Uranium's development team wrote that they believed the attack had been the result of leaked information.

entries.title: $80 million taken from EasyFi lending platform
entries.body: Hackers compromised a computer belonging to EasyFi founder Ankitt Gaur, accessing his <button class="define-target" id="private-key">private keys</button> which allowed them to transfer $6 million in <button class="define-target" id="stablecoin">stablecoins</button> and $120 million worth of EASY. The price of EASY crashed as a result of the low liquidity, limiting the hacker's total payout to around $80 million. EasyFi followed the breach with a <button class="define-target" id="fork">hard fork</button> to "EZ 2.0", and compensated users with a mix of stablecoins and "IOU tokens" that could later be redeemed for discounted EZ.

entries.title: FTX loses $800 million to MobileCoin market manipulation
entries.body:
At some point in April 2021, a trader on the FTX cryptocurrency exchange successfully exploited the firm for around $800 million. They were able to take positions in relatively illiquid crypto tokens, including MobileCoin and BTMX, then manipulate the token prices to appear much higher than their true market value (for example, MobileCoin spiked to $70 a token, rather than around $6). Using these falsely high-valued tokens as collateral, the trader was able to borrow around $800 million in more liquid tokens, abandoning the relatively valueless collateral on the exchange.

During the October 2023 criminal trial of FTX founder and CEO Sam Bankman-Fried, he gave more detail on how the exploit took place, and admitted that he personally had disabled FTX's automatic systems for this account. Though he intended to closely monitor the account to prevent any losses to FTX, he said that it was actually his actions that allowed the trader to drain such a massive quantity of assets from the exchange.

Prosecutors alleged that Bankman-Fried later had his cryptocurrency trading firm, Alameda Research, shoulder the loss, saying that he'd hoped it would be less visible on Alameda's balance sheets than on FTX's.

entries.title: Social token platform Roll hacked for $5.7 million
entries.body: <button class="define-target" id="private-key">Private keys</button> for <button class="define-target" id="hot-wallet">hot wallets</button> on the Roll network were compromised, allowing the theft of around $5.7 million from various "social tokens". "Friends With Benefits", an a16z-backed <button class="define-target" id="dao">DAO</button> with an associated token that allows those who are approved by the DAO and can afford the ~$8,000 entrance fee access to exclusive parties, was one of the tokens affected, and it tanked in value by about 96%. Roll apologized and announced a fund to help those affected, though the $500,000 fund was only a small fraction of the money lost.

entries.body: A contract exploit allowed a hacker to <button class="define-target" id="mint">mint</button> almost 60 million PAID tokens (priced at around $160 million based on the value before the attack) on the PAID Network. The hacker then made off with about $3 million in Ethereum from their efforts. The attack caused the PAID token to crash about 88% in value over the course of a day, from around $2.86 to $0.32.

links.linkText: "Alpha Homora exploited for $37.5M"

entries.body: A hacker was able to code a <button class="define-target" id="smart-contract">smart contract</button> that tricked C.R.E.A.M. into believing it was from a trusted source. They were then able to make off with $37.5 million worth of Ethereum and stablecoins in what was only the first of several major exploits of the platform in 2021.
